# Ark Financial Holding To Acquire Cooper Lake Financial Corp.

Pulse 2.0
Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn

Ark Financial Holding, Inc. has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Cooper Lake Financial Corporation, the holding company of The First National Bank in Cooper. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including shareholder approval and required regulatory approvals.

Following the completion of the acquisition, Ark plans to inject additional capital into The First National Bank in Cooper to support a multi-year modernization initiative. The investment program will focus on upgrading the bank’s technology infrastructure, expanding digital banking services, and introducing enhanced digital payments capabilities for customers. [...] Sheshunoff & Co. Investment Banking served as financial advisor to Ark Financial Holding in the transaction, while Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton LLP acted as legal counsel. Cooper Lake Financial Corporation and The First National Bank in Cooper were advised by Robert N. Flowers of Bradley Arant Boult Cummings LLP and Jay Garrett.

KEY QUOTES:

“This new partnership with Ark will provide the bank with the resources to invest in modernizing our technology infrastructure, including digital banking services. Our customers will continue to see the same faces and receive the same care and service as they always have when they walk into the bank.”

Tim Gregory, President and CEO, Cooper Lake Financial Corporation and The First National Bank in Cooper [...] Founded more than a century ago, The First National Bank in Cooper is the oldest bank in Delta County, Texas. Under the proposed ownership, the bank will continue operating from its current location in Cooper and maintain its commitment to serving local customers and surrounding communities. Customers are expected to experience no disruption to deposit accounts, loan relationships, branch hours, or daily banking operations, while continuing to work with the same banking team.

Ark Financial Holding said the acquisition aligns with its expertise in digital banking, digital payments, and financial technology, enabling the organization to support the bank’s long-term growth while preserving its community banking heritage.

results.title: Financial Services M&A Trends 2026 | Fintent
results.content:
Payments technology (1.62x, 1,291 companies) is the strongest M&A signal in the sector. The public record has already caught up in the large-cap tier: Capital One acquired Brex for $5.15 billion in January 2026 (pwc.com), Mastercard bought stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK for up to $1.8 billion in March (forbes.com), and Nuvei agreed to acquire Payoneer for $2.75 billion in June (bloomberg.com). What the index adds is the tier below those headlines, where the 1,291 tracked middle-market names sit. So what: this is where sell-side mandates in financial services are most likely to originate over the next 18 to 24 months, and a coverage list built only from announced payments deals is already a year behind. [...] ## Frequently asked questions

### Which financial services sub-sector has the strongest M&A signal in 2026?

Payments technology, at 1.62x M&A Propensity across 1,291 tracked companies. The public record agrees: Capital One acquired Brex for $5.15 billion in January 2026, Mastercard bought BVNK for up to $1.8 billion in March, and Nuvei agreed to acquire Payoneer for $2.75 billion in June.

### Why do community banks rank low when bank M&A headlines are so active?

Because announced deals and deal preparation are measured at different points in time. Regulators approved bank mergers in 2025 at the fastest pace since 1990, but those deals were prepared under the prior regime. At 0.62x, community banks are not showing the preparation behaviour a re-loading pipeline would produce. [...] The public deal record supports the top of the table more readily than the bottom. Payments produced three transactions above $1.8 billion in the first half of 2026 alone. Tax and accounting platforms generated roughly 900 add-on acquisitions off fewer than 200 sponsor platforms in 2025 (cfobrew.com). Investment consulting saw Neuberger Berman absorb McKinsey's $26 billion MIO unit in March 2026 (consultingmag.com). These are not quiet corners of the market.
